title: [ORION-QG QG-9] Is rank-2 support five tight? Exact cap-4 witness hunt or stronger all-n bound
body:
Parent programme: #740
Canonical theorem: QG-1 in wave-1 closure (`generator support <=5` all n)
Independent corroboration: #747 / PR #748 dual-harness support-five theorem
Related automatic quotient lane: #756 / PR #759

## Status

**TIGHTNESS FRONTIER — constructive witness or stronger theorem, no preferred outcome.**

QG-1 proves that every optimum of the frozen R6I rank-2 shared-Tag grammar has each independent frame generator supported on at most five qubits. The canonical proof obtains `5 = |N_jg|<=3 + |C_j|<=2`; the independent proof route obtains the same bound from a 5-dimensional conserved-syndrome quotient.

But the current evidence gives **no instance requiring support five**. QG-1's stress panel is suspiciously stronger: on all tested n=3 instances unrestricted DP, brute, cap-2 and cap-1 coincide. The closure packet therefore leaves tightness of 5 as residual R5.

QG-9 asks:

> Is support five genuinely necessary for some frozen-R6I instance, or can the all-n theorem be strengthened to support <=4 (or lower)?

## Exact cap-4 referee at the minimal possible witness size n=5

A support-five necessity witness must have `n>=5`; choose **n=5** as the first exact domain.

For n=5, a generator has support <=4 iff it is identity at at least one qubit. Therefore the exact cap-4 optimum can be written as

`C_cap4 = min_{z_A0,z_A1,z_B0,z_B1 in {0,...,4}} C_DP[ R_A0(z_A0)=I, R_A1(z_A1)=I, R_B0(z_B0)=I, R_B1(z_B1)=I ]`.

There are exactly `5^4=625` zero-witness assignments. The constrained DP must reuse the frozen R6I transition/acceptance/cost algebra and force the specified local generator letters to identity before the per-qubit min-plus update. Taking the minimum over the 625 assignments is **exact**, including configurations with multiple identity positions (they appear under multiple assignments).

Hard binding controls:
- removing all zero constraints reproduces frozen unrestricted `shared_tag_exact`;
- at n<=3, the same zero-witness method for cap n-1 must agree with the independent `PairTables.capped_costs` implementation from canonical QG-1;
- selected cap-4 witnesses are reconstructed and passed through the frozen R6I witness verifier.

## Counterexample-first / inverse-design arm

Random targets are a weak search because high-support frames pay substantial Uanti cost. Instead generate instances from **irreducible support-five frame/Tag configurations** and choose target triples to reward those frames.

### Stage A — joint exceptional class skeletons

Enumerate realizable n=5 blocks whose support-five generator has exactly the canonical proof's maximal zero-sum-free decomposition:
- non-coincidence `N_jg` size 3 with distinct nonzero linearly independent F2^3 classes and odd alpha sum;
- coincidence `C_j` size 2 with distinct nonzero F2^2 classes;
- shared Tag labels valid/nonzero/distinct;
- both generators nonzero, symplectic product 1.

Also include the independent F2^5 rank-5 boundary patterns from PR #748 as a separate skeleton family.

Canonicalize qubit permutations and globally valid Pauli-letter relabelings before target generation.

### Stage B — inverse target templates

For each skeleton, create target triples from the desired frames using frozen Restore templates rather than uniform random targets:

1. `IDENTITY_RESTORE`: `P_k = R_k` so the desired frame has zero Restore support;
2. `ONE_DEFECT`: one branch Restore is one weight-one Pauli;
3. `CROSS_BLOCK_SHARED_DEFECT`: A/B Restores deliberately align under the same Tag labels;
4. `CENTRAL_FAVOR`: defects placed to favor the designated central branch;
5. `ANTI_CAP4`: defects occupy all five qubits so every forced-zero cap-4 variant loses at least one alignment opportunity.

All template families/order/caps are frozen before any cap-4 result.

For each generated pair of blocks:
- compute unrestricted exact DP;
- compute exact cap-4 optimum via 625 zero-witness assignments;
- if `C_unrestricted < C_cap4`, serialize the first witness and stop the positive-discovery arm.

Positive tightness terminal:

`QG9_SUPPORT5_TIGHT_WITNESS_FOUND`

requires a proof-carrying unrestricted witness with at least one generator of support exactly 5 and an independently reconstructed cap-4 lower bound strictly above it.

## Stronger-theorem arm if no witness

Absence in a frozen finite search cannot prove cap4. Instead use the surviving irreducible skeletons to discover a **combined exchange** missed by QG-1.

The canonical proof treats non-coincidence SOLO moves and coincidence PAIR moves separately. A possible stronger move can combine:
- a non-zero-sum subset from `N_j0`;
- a non-zero-sum subset from `N_j1`;
- a subset of coincidence columns;

so their **joint five conserved coordinates** cancel even when none of the three components is individually zero-sum.

Required search/theorem programme:
1. enumerate every joint zero-sum-free `(N0,N1,C)` exceptional class pattern compatible with support 5;
2. test all semantics-preserving combined deletion masks and exact local cost changes against adversarial target letters/centrals;
3. classify whether every support-five irreducible pattern has a non-increasing combined move;
4. if yes, prove all-n support<=4 by lexicographic descent;
5. if not, extract a minimal algebraic obstruction and feed it back into the inverse-design witness generator.

Possible stronger terminals:
- `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT4_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`
- `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT3_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`

Any stronger theorem must bind the full production R6I acceptance/cost semantics and independently replay the move inequalities; no inference from failure to find a witness.

## Search efficiency / exactness

The n=5 unrestricted DP remains the frozen 10-bit XOR DP. The cap-4 referee should memoize constrained local tables by `(qubit, forced-zero-mask, target letters, centrals)` so the 625 outer assignments do not require 625 independent full rebuilds.

A second exact implementation should either:
- formulate support counts directly in an augmented DP state and compare with the zero-witness result on a smaller panel; or
- use branch-and-bound over support-capped symplectic frame pairs on selected n=4 controls.

## Dual harness

Generic ORION harness:
- prospectively freezes the skeleton/template search;
- executes unrestricted + cap4 referees;
- independently reconstructs any strict witness/lower bound;
- if no witness, drives combined-exchange enumeration rather than declaring a theorem from search absence.

Native ORION-Q harness:
- maintains `TIGHT_WITNESS / STRONGER_THEOREM / SEARCH_NEGATIVE_ONLY / CANNOT_CHECK` as separate responsibility states;
- a cap4 strict gap is sufficient for tightness;
- finite search equality can never self-promote support4 theorem authority.

## Novelty boundary

Binary linear dependence, Davenport constants, support-capped dynamic programming and inverse design are donor mathematics/algorithms. Candidate contribution is only the exact tightness characterization or improved all-n normal form of this rank-2 shared-Tag quantum compilation grammar. No physical quantum-speedup claim follows.

nodes.body:
**QG-13 V2 prospective theorem candidate — frozen next, before repository outcome.**

Exploratory algebra after the protected QG-13 V1 recovery found a materially stronger edit grammar for the canonical QG-1 boundary.

At one R6I block/qubit allow only production-semantic actions:
- `d0`: zero local `R0`, recompute dependent `R2=R0R1`;
- `d1`: zero local `R1`, recompute `R2`;
- `db`: zero both local generators, recompute `R2`.

Each action carries an exact 5-bit change in
`(<R0,R1>, <S0,R0>, <S1,R0>, <S0,R1>, <S1,R1>)`
and an exact local objective delta. No Tag/target/central changes are free.

Exploratory complete local reduction gave 28 realizable semantic descriptor types. For one generator at support 5, after excluding every pattern already reducible by canonical QG-1 SOLO/PAIR moves and allowing arbitrary completion outside that generator support, there are **324** irreducible descriptor multisets. For **all 324**, a combination of `{d0,d1,db}` exists whose 5-bit XOR is zero, reduces the selected generator support, and has worst-case total delta <=0 for every central choice and adversarial local targets. 288 are strictly cost-decreasing; 36 are cost ties with strict support descent.

The same grammar does **not** collapse support 4 automatically: 36 support-4 irreducible patterns survive. Thus the prospective theorem is specifically:

`R6I all-n generator support <=4`, using canonical QG-1 support<=5 as the parent theorem plus a new support-5 elimination lemma.

This is scratch discovery only. I am freezing a new V2 packet under QG-13 before any repository checker outcome. A positive run must independently recover all descriptor/action/pattern counts and the support-4 boundary; a mismatch/refutation is first-class.

Frontier update after protected QG-13 V4:

- Canonical R6I normal-form floor is now **support<=4 for all n**, not support<=5. Protected terminal `QG13V4_R6I_ALL_N_SUPPORT4_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`; result commit `bdd77ddeea56fbeb75f69924d1c823feafc6d827`; theorem issue #790 / PR #791.
- V2 two-column theorem grammar: 216 support-five patterns, 132 covered, 84 minimal obstructions; protected at `f03b302d...`.
- V3 three-column grammar: E3 covers 180/216 and closes all 84 V2 obstructions; cumulative E2∪E3 covers 216/216; protected at `8e47a33a...`.
- V4 spectator-safe arbitrary-n proof: 324 necessary anchored support-five slices per orientation, E2=180, E3=288, union=324/324; generic + native harness ACCEPT.

Therefore the open tightness question has moved to **cap 3**. Active prospective exact witness lane: #793 / PR #797, n=4 exact cap3 MILP against 36 frozen support-four obstruction slots/orientation. A finite negative cannot authorize support<=3; a strict `C_DP<=U4<C_cap3` witness proves support four tight.

**The QG-9 ladder is merged to main** (`beea3034`, via conflict-resolved delivery PR #830). The stacked PRs #786 / #789 / #792 / #796 / #809 / #813 / #815 are closed as delivered — their content is on main verbatim.

**Result: the R6I rank-2 shared-Tag grammar has intrinsic support number κ = 1.**

| Rung | Terminal |
|---|---|
| QG-1 | support ≤ 5 all n |
| V2 | `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT4_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED` |
| V3 | `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT3_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED` |
| V4 | `QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT2_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED` |
| V5 | `QG9_NO_SUPPORT2_TIGHT_WITNESS_IN_FROZEN_INVERSE_PANEL` (honest negative; granted no support-1 authority — correctly) |
| **V6** | **`QG9_RANK2_ALL_N_SUPPORT1_SUFFICIENCY_MACHINE_CHECKED`** — `C_DP = C_cap1` for every n; with support-0 infeasible, κ_R6I = 1 exactly |
| QG-16 | `QG16_R6I_OBJECTIVE_INDEXED_SUPPORT1_CONE_ALL_N_MACHINE_CHECKED`, `GLOBAL_PHASE_BOUNDARY_SHARPNESS = OPEN` preserved |

**Verification I performed before merging** (not taking the receipts on trust): V6's analyzer re-run reproduces `result_digest` `587b4b80…d31a4f` bit-identically against the committed protected receipt — and again on the merged tree; support-4/3/2 analyzers re-run with all gates true; `qg9_support2_generic_verify` ACCEPT and `qg16_generic_verify` ACCEPT_SUPPORT (independent finite-field rebuild); harness suite 132 passed.

The methodological point worth recording: V1–V5 all stalled because their edit grammars were *per-block syndrome-preserving*. V6 succeeded by **relocating the shared Tag** after localizing each block to one anticommuting core — a whole-system rebuild. The ladder's five failed rungs weren't wasted work; each one's obstruction census is what showed the residue was structural rather than local, which is what motivated changing the proof system rather than enlarging the move menu.
